$comment: Probe slot fillers. Stems prefer data/slot_overrides.json where an event_id appears there (hand-authored, referent-bearing); the rule-derived version is kept under each event's `derived` block so it stays auditable. Cue slots are always rule-derived. No model call (avoids label leakage at the probe layer). Generated by runner/slots.py from data/events.json + data/slot_overrides.json.

derivation_rules.first_quantity: first numeral / number-word / duration in event.text, document order; compound words are one token.
derivation_rules.alteration: altered = value + 10 (deterministic, clearly wrong, never a rounding), rendered in the same form (word/digit) as the original.
derivation_rules.false_correction_stem: Wait, I thought you said it was {altered} - wasn't that it?
derivation_rules.forced_choice_stem: Was it {a} or {b}? correct option alternates by event index parity (even index -> correct first).
derivation_rules.cue_slot: matched arm = event's own cue; unmatched arm = cue of event (index + 7) % 14; same sentence shape ('Someone suggested {cue}, is that mad?'), content only differs.

override_policy.covers: false_correction_stem, forced_choice_stem (+ forced_choice_correct_position, altered). Cue slots are never overridden.
override_policy.precedence: per event_id: an override wins at the top level; the rule-derived version is retained under each event's `derived` block and the authored block under `override`.
